idiom_name: interface delegation with the by clause
implementation_notes: class CircleShape(private val renderer: Renderer, ...) : Renderer by renderer is the whole pattern: the by clause stores the delegate and the compiler generates every interface member as a forwarding call, which is exactly the boilerplate the classic structure exists to remove, and an explicit override replaces a generated member where the abstraction adds behaviour. Delegation is captured once at construction - the language specification is explicit that the delegate expression is evaluated a single time - so runtime implementor swapping needs a real field rather than the by clause. The hand-written abstract-class-plus-interface form is still justified when the abstraction must expose operations outside the delegated interface, or when two delegated interfaces share member names and need an explicit resolution.
pitfalls: The delegate expression is evaluated once at construction (the spec is explicit), so a var property used as a delegate does not change the object's behaviour afterwards - runtime swapping needs an explicit field.

Overrides in the delegating class are not visible to the delegate: the delegate can only call its own implementations, so designs in which the delegate calls back into the abstraction need an explicit reference.
Two delegated interfaces that declare the same member require an explicit override, otherwise the compiler rejects the class.
